anya (devex): Heads-up: onboarding sampleapp produced duplicate invoices when auth rotated mid-submit. Short repro below, need SDK guidance on safe resume patterns.

mike (sdk): quick Qs: where are you storing pending state and what do you replay?

anya (devex): We keep a pending JSON in localStorage including body and idempotencyKey so reload resumes. Code: `localStorage.pending = JSON.stringify({key, body})` then we re-POST on load.

deepa (platform): storing full body is risky. If token refresh happens and the original request finishes late you can double-create. Server might return late 201 while replay also creates 201.

anya (devex): Timeline: t0 POST, t1 auth refresh started, t2 client replays, t3 original finally 201, t4 replay 201.

mike (sdk): recommended pattern: persist only minimal metadata (idempotency key, endpoint), and on resume call an idempotency-check endpoint (HEAD /resource/idempotency/{key}) before re-POSTing. If server says "in_progress" poll; if "complete" return result; if "missing" create new attempt with new key.

anya (devex): Can SDK offer a helper for that? We want consistent behavior across sampleapps.

mike (sdk): yes — proposing `sdk.idempotency.resume(pending)` that does: check -> poll if needed -> create new attempt if missing. Also emit `auth:refresh` events so resumers can pause replay during rotations.

deepa (platform): add note: treat 202 as in-flight; avoid blind replays for accepted-but-not-complete responses. And prefer server-scoped namespaces in keys (clientId:key) to avoid cross-client collisions.

ci-bot: CI: sampleapps/onboarding #118 passed :white_check_mark:

anya (devex): thanks. I'll update the sampleapp to stop persisting raw bodies, add the resume helper, and include an e2e that simulates token rotation. PR incoming and will tag "sdk-idempotency".

mike (sdk): cool — please add a tiny README blurb: "persist metadata only; check idempotency before replay; subscribe to auth events". That should reduce these dupes significantly.

anya (devex): will do. Appreciated!
